statement_verbatim:
statement: >-
  Each authored area of the canonical tree — `docs/`, `docs/purpose/`, `docs/architecture/`,
  `docs/architecture/decisions/`, `docs/archive/` — MUST contain an `index.adoc`.
  Other canonical filenames are defined when useful and are NOT instantiated merely to satisfy an
  empty taxonomy (spec 2 §4).

statement: >-
  A documentation artifact declared at RATIFY MUST name a `path` that begins `docs/` and ends
  `.adoc`; an artifact with `action: archive` MUST name a `path` beneath `docs/archive/`. Core stores
  these paths as opaque strings and never interprets them (companion §3); interpreting them is this
  extension's job, because only the extension knows the tree.

statement: >-
  A file authored beneath `docs/` MUST be AsciiDoc (`.adoc`). An authored `.md` beneath `docs/`,
  outside the generated `docs/dist/` tree, is a violation. This is the format half of the
  documentation model handoff spec 2 §4 names; it is an EXTENSION obligation because core is
  forbidden to know what a `.adoc` is (companion §4, *Deliberately excluded*).

statement: >-
  No two authored documents beneath `docs/` may declare the same `:doc-id:`. Uniqueness is what makes
  `doc-id` an identity rather than a label, and it is the precondition for resolving any relationship
  edge to exactly one target (spec 2 §5.1).

statement: >-
  Every relationship attribute on an authored document (`:decides:`, `:supersedes:`, `:implements:`,
  `:depends-on:`) MUST name a `doc-id` that some document in the corpus actually declares. A target
  outside that set is a REPORTED finding. It is NEVER synthesized into a node, and never silently
  dropped. This is the one hard requirement of spec 2 §5.4 and the flagship rule of this extension.

statement: >-
  An authored `.adoc` beneath `docs/` MUST declare both a `:doc-id:` and a `:status:` attribute with
  non-empty values. `doc-id` is the document's node identity in the relationship graph (spec 2 §5.1);
  `status` is what makes the current-versus-historical boundary readable at all.

statement: >-
  When a repository documents itself (`docs/` exists) and its plan declares journeys or flow routers,
  `docs/purpose/journeys/` MUST contain exactly what `atdd-bun docs journeys` generates from `plan/`:
  `index.adoc` and one SVG per journey map, per journey's nominal path, and per routed user/system flow. A missing,
  stale, hand-edited, or extra file is a violation.

statement: >-
  The corpus MUST render with asciidoctor, and every internal cross-reference MUST resolve. A build
  failure or an unresolvable internal reference is a FAIL. An ABSENT toolchain, or a build failure
  the capability cannot attribute to a specific document, is `COULD_NOT_CHECK` — never `PASS`, and
  never `FAIL` (spec 2 §3, *What the capability owes core*, and §7).

statement: >-
  Any path in the change set beneath `docs/`, outside `docs/dist/`, MUST be covered by an artifact in
  the documentation declaration. An undeclared documentation change is a violation. This rule lives in
  the extension and NOT in core, because it requires knowing `docs/` (spec 2 §4; companion §4,
  *Deliberately excluded*).

statement: 'Feature names are seeded from product capability produce/consume artifacts: identify the artifact, determine
  its type, pick a type-specific verb, choose an object from the artifact''s domain/resource, and combine
  as {verb}-{object}.'
statement: Each feature is registered under exactly one product capability's _features.yaml manifest.

statement: A feature is the smallest independently-verifiable slice of a product capability's behavior
  — a bounded capability that declares a URN, a status, and a non-empty acceptance
  section, links to exactly one product capability, closes a feedback loop, and stays within its
  size limits. This node is an advisory semantic anchor — it enforces nothing directly;
  the enforceable parts of this meaning are decomposed into the constraint/rule nodes
  that require it.
statement: Estimate the architectural footprint from DESIRED OUTCOMES, interfaces, and component layers.

statement: 'A feature marked kind: feedback-loop must declare at least one SMOKE acceptance with a close_the_loop
  block containing consumer_reacted and drift_resolved.'

statement: 'An optional feature `kind:` classifies the system archetype; kind: feedback-loop marks a producer->consumer
  correction loop (detect+emit, receive+react, predicate no longer fires).'

statement: 'A docs-only feedback-loop feature may suppress the close-the-loop rule inline on the kind:
  line.'

statement: Architectural footprint = sum(component.count x weight[component.type]), rounded UP, mapped
  to a size bracket.

statement: Group DESIRED OUTCOMES into a feature by shared step, dimension, object, or coherent user story (<=10
  per group); avoid miscellaneous buckets.
